02 · WhyThe Principles I Work By
The Marketing Playbook

Six lenses behind the results — one connected system: engaging the customer, reading the market, prioritizing the account, activating the ecosystem, executing the strategy, and building the system that lets what works repeat and expand.

CustomerCustomer-centric engagement

Core idea

Understand the customer deeply → create meaningful engagement → create business opportunity.

Proof

Executive roundtables, C-level forums and multi-year field programs were each planned around one goal: a qualified business conversation with the right stakeholders.

Principle in practice

Customers and partners are the ecosystem — not the audience.Both persona-mapped buying committees and the APAC partner incentive program started from this customer-engagement view.

Market 0→1Vertical GTM & market development

Core idea

Understand the market → identify where to play → build a GTM approach.

Proof

At Zebra, built a four-year vertical GTM platform in industrial automation (2022–2026) from a single reframed field event — one narrative, one pipeline model, and one measurement standard where none existed before. Earlier, at Schneider Electric, led Smart Factory + Automation World 2016 company-wide across business units.

Principle in practice

Strategy earns its value in execution.Standardized annual operating model Inquiry capture → sales handoff → pipeline tracking → next-year follow-through

AccountABM & account-based growth

Core idea

Account prioritization → buying group mapping → sales & marketing alignment → personalized content & engagement → pipeline development.

Proof

Prioritized strategic accounts by fit, urgency, and expansion potential, mapped buying committees down to the persona level, and translated account strategy into locally relevant messaging — in 2025, 10 target accounts produced $350K in ABM closed-won revenue.

Principle in practice

Marketing is momentum, not activity.$5.36M in direct-sourced closed-won revenue came from planning every program against pipeline, with lead-quality metrics shared with Sales and Inside Sales.

Ecosystem 1→10Partner ecosystem & regional growth

Core idea

Partner → ecosystem → joint GTM → market expansion.

Proof

Designed and launched the first APAC-wide channel incentive program, turning partner relationships from a co-marketing line item into a repeatable regional growth mechanism scaled across six markets.

Principle in practice

Great GTM happens between functions.Regional strategy, local execution, sales, and partners only move together when someone connects them — that connective role is where most of this career has been spent.

ExecutionStrategic execution

Core idea

Ambiguity → direction → action → business results.

Proof

As the sole regional marketer across two countries — and later inside APAC HQ — connected global strategy to local reality: clarifying the business question, aligning stakeholders I didn't manage, and turning direction into a cadence that could be measured and repeated.

Principle in practice

I don't wait for clarity. I create it.As the sole regional marketer for Korea and the Philippines, there was no existing playbook — the demand generation model was built while it was being run.

Scale 0→1→10Regional expansion & scalable systems

Core idea

Local insight → localize → pilot → build the model → standardize → regional expansion → scale.

Proof

Working across Korea and the Philippines inside a broader APAC structure, and collaborating on APAC-driven regional initiatives, I've taken what worked in one market and turned it into a repeatable operating model — including the first APAC channel incentive program, later scaled across six markets.

Principle in practice

Start small. Learn fast. Scale what works.The APAC channel incentive program began as a single-market idea and became a repeatable mechanism across six markets.

Three revenue decisions AI improves

Predict pipeline & account readiness

Use engagement, intent, firmographic, and historical performance signals to identify where demand is likely to convert into pipeline — before it surfaces through traditional lead capture.

Personalize buying-group journeys

Messaging tailored to executive, operations, technical, finance and partner stakeholders Content and engagement personalized by buying-committee role

Guide sales next-best actions

Connect marketing intelligence to sales timing, follow-up priority, and opportunity context — so each marketing signal leads to a defined sales follow-up.

Challenge

From event execution to business results

Field events needed to become more than visibility programs. The business needed measurable opportunity creation, stakeholder engagement and consistent sales follow-up.

Strategy

Rebuilt as a Repeatable Growth Platform

Positioned Automation World as a structured revenue platform connecting executive engagement, cross-BU alignment and solution storytelling — run for four editions.

Execution

Operationalizing the Sales Follow-up Loop

Ran sustained multi-year event leadership with inquiry capture, sales coordination, performance tracking, and disciplined commercial handoff — each year building on the previous year's contacts and pipeline.

Result

A four-year revenue platform (2022–2026)

$17.7M total lead value · 3,289 inquiries · 19 closed-won deals · $3.4M closed-won revenue (2022–2025)

"An event is not the outcome. It is where revenue opportunities start."

Global priorities, local reality

Convert global and APAC priorities into local country plans, market messaging, and execution cadences that fit customer behavior — maintaining pipeline accountability across diverse market dynamics.

Multi-country operating coverage

    About Sungmee

    Turning business questions into marketing plans — and plans into measurable pipeline.

    My 20-year career began at a Korean startup and grew through global technology companies — Dassault Systèmes, Cisco, Schneider Electric and Zebra Technologies — across Demand Generation, ABM, Channel Marketing, Partner Marketing, Field Marketing and Regional Marketing. Most recently, I've led Korea and Philippines field marketing and collaborated on regional programs at Zebra's Singapore APAC HQ.

    Most of my work starts with an open brief — a market to enter, an account list to prioritize, a partner program to rebuild. I use market data, CRM data and Sales input to decide where to focus first.

    My strength is connecting strategy and execution: define the business problem → find the starting point → align stakeholders → standardize what works. I run every program as my own business, earning trust with Sales, regional teams and partners through clear communication and consistent results.

    What I'm most proud of is not just the results, but what I've learned along the way — building new programs, navigating challenges, and finding better ways to work.

    "I may not have every answer on day one, but I will take responsibility for finding it, testing it and making it work."
